newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SWIMMING-HUNGARY SWIMMING TEAM HEAD REELECTED AFTER SCANDAL.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-HUNGARY SWIMMING TEAM HEAD REELECTED AFTER SCANDAL.

text.p: Tamas Gyarfas, who was reelected head of the Hungarian Swimming Federation (HSF), at the weekend, said on Monday frauds such as the "phantom" qualifying meet over which he resigned will not be repeated.
"I will personally see that such things never happen again," Gyarfas told Reuters after he was elected president of the HSF on Saturday by 65 votes to two.
Gyarfas quit his post after allegations that half of Hungary's Olympic swimming team competed in Atlanta on the basis of a qualifying meet which never took place.
When he resigned, Gyarfas said he had no previous knowledge of the affair.
The general secretary of HSF, Jozsef Ruza later admitted of sending the counterfeit qualifying sheets.
Ruza was also reelected to his post on Saturday.
"Everybody involved was willing to take as much of the blame as possible," Gyarfas said, adding that he woyld accpet the re-election.
"To leave my post at this stage would not be the proper thing to do," he said. "The federation needs to stick together."

Although he described the forgeries as an "inadmissible, grave mistake" he said the fraud did not result in Hungarian swimmers taking the place of any other nation's athletes at the Olympics as each country had its own quota of places.
